findings.topic: Ordinary MXF imports the own physical file descriptor SampleRate
anchors: own SourceMob descriptor/CreateDescriptor/ConvertDescriptorFromAAF: prior native Kind receipt
findings.evidence: The ordinary managed MXF route creates/imports the selected physical SourceMob own EssenceDescriptor. Picture DID property import calls the file-descriptor base, which gets typed SampleRate on that descriptor and stores its internal rate. Verified DID/CDCI vtables resolve SetRate/GetExactEditRate to base file-descriptor state. No universal interlace halving, project-rate substitution or timecode nominal-base substitution occurs in this selected rate block.

findings.topic: Native internal aliases differ from explicit wire rationals
findings.evidence: The importer preserves denominator-1 input as an internal integer and recognizes finite exact rational aliases (including 30000/1001, 24000/1001, 60000/1001); remaining input takes signed numerator/denominator double division into ExactEditRateFromFloat. GetExactEditRate returns stored internal state; GetRate calls the literal-decimal EditRateFromExactEditRate. An internal getter name alone does not establish literal versus effective NTSC timing. Bella should retain a valid explicit raw MXF rational directly, while the separately approved MDB legacy interpreter stays at its own adapter boundary. No universal exact import/export bijection is claimed.

findings.topic: Physical video metadata publication uses own rate explicitly
findings.evidence: The picture metadata publisher calls the base publisher, obtains the same own physical descriptor internal rate, converts it with RationalFromExactEditRate and publishes rational SampleRate alongside own EssenceLength. This connects a physical metadata boundary, not an app table Frame Rate selection or a guarantee that every supported wrapping sample is one complete picture frame.

findings.topic: FrameLayout is imported and retained separately
anchors: DID typed digital-image descriptor FrameLayout getter 0x3823e4
toolkit getter slot 0x2e4960 on interface point 0x2e4900, method offset 0x60
DID stored layout at this+0x2a0 around 0x382524
findings.evidence: DID import obtains typed FrameLayout separately from base file SampleRate and uses layout, raster and codec context for picture geometry. Layout and codec-specific compatibility branches exist; observed geometry halving must not be confused with a rate-halving instruction. FrameLayout, raw descriptor rate, physical unit coverage and codec-wrapper rate belong to distinct contexts.

findings.topic: A separate codec sample-to-frame conversion exists, with different enum numbering
findings.evidence: The codec helper halves the signed numerator (integer divide by two, denominator unchanged) only for internal DF_FrameLayout_t value 2. The binary names that internal value FL_SeparateFields. The DynamicCompression accessor supplies a codec-wrapper layout and codec-wrapper rational; another direct caller initializes target-format globals from a target VCID. A separate enum converter maps internal DF layout 2 to the CM-style layout value 1. Therefore internal value 2 is not the same as raw MXF FrameLayout value 2, and the helper is not evidence to halve every raw interlaced MXF descriptor SampleRate. The direct call scan does not exclude indirect calls elsewhere.

findings.topic: Video wrapper construction is codec/raster context, not raw rate guessing
findings.evidence: Video format wrapper construction obtains a rate through the media descriptor, reconstructs internal exact state and publishes its rational to a VCID/format wrapper. Later geometry/layout and codec logic is separate. This supports keeping native rate conversion boundaries explicit; it does not establish a universal raw-MXF-rate-to-Frame-Rate GUI mapping or justify copying floating-point detours into Bella.

findings.topic: Track EditRate and composition editing rate are separately imported
findings.evidence: The composition importer separately selects an editing rate, and its mob-slot helper obtains a picture track EditRate through the typed TimelineMobSlot interface. The helper has additional header/physical-mob and import-context routes. These component/composition clock paths must not be silently substituted for the own file descriptor rate; no universal precedence between every native composition clock and the GUI Frame Rate column is established.

findings.topic: Audio and timecode clocks do not fill a physical-video Frame Rate
findings.evidence: The preceding native Duration audit proves that audio imports separate AudioSamplingRate and can keep additional source/editing/timecode clocks with container/override-specific transformations. Preface.ProjectEditRate is separately recorded header editing metadata, and a timecode nominal base plus drop mode controls numbering. None is established as a universal physical-video frame-rate substitute. Bella audio Frame Rate remains blank under the existing agreement; this audit does not reopen display-duration or source-priority rules.

mediaComposer.settledBellaBoundary: MDB Frame Rate remains first; an independently required header read may supply an otherwise unavailable rate under the existing agreed source boundary, without a Frame-Rate-only media open. Exact numeric/rational retention, separate audio Sample Rate and audio Frame Rate blank remain agreed. New detailed MXF Frame Rate interpretation rules are research/proposal only until user approval. No unrelated Duration/DF formatting changes.
limits: No complete Media Composer GUI Frame Rate-column source, native UI formatting/default path or universal all-format parity trace is established.
The ordinary own descriptor import/publication boundary is proved. Codec-wrapper SeparateFields conversion is separately proved; it is not a universal raw MXF FrameLayout rule.

sourceFindings.detail: Primer/schema identifies FileDescriptor.SampleRate and Track.EditRate separately as Rational. Rational is an eight-byte compound of signed big-endian Int32 numerator followed by denominator, decoded exactly; complete fixed size is checked. FrameLayout is a separate Uint8.

Current projector requires a unique active ContentStorage ECD -> full-ID SourcePackage match within its partition, then a complete descriptor relationship. It recursively traverses MultipleDescriptor children and projects each supported technical descriptor. It does not filter FrameRate descriptors by LinkedTrackID; the latter is consulted in the separate missing-ContainerDuration file-track fallback.

Video is identified by current registered picture ancestry OR PictureEssenceCoding property presence. If audio and video meanings coexist the technical projection returns unresolved. Otherwise FrameRate is exactly the same descriptor FileDescriptor.SampleRate when its positive numerator/denominator are usable. No Track.EditRate comparison, no field-to-frame conversion, no FrameLayout-based halving, no Avid MDB decimal alias conversion, no master/project/nominal timecode fallback for this column.

unique rejects an unreadable/invalid property or conflicting repeated decoded values. Positive rational validation gates the FrameRate observation. All MultipleDescriptor branches can contribute; equal-rank incompatible fractions resolve to unavailable, rather than first descriptor wins. Equivalent positive fractions compare by exact Int64 cross-products. Descriptor/property absence or damage does not drop the physical row.

sourceFindings.topic: Current preference and I/O differ from Bella
sourceFindings.detail: Current selection prefers MXF/OMF FrameRate over MDB. Missing required video FrameRate is one scheduling reason to open a media header. Bella has already chosen usable MDB first and already-read own header only if MDB is unusable; FrameRate alone must not trigger that header read.

MXF audio projects concrete AudioSamplingRate to SampleRate and produces no FrameRate observation. Its internal Preface editing/display clock is only Duration context, not visible audio FrameRate. Current adapter itself does not apply a Kind-based blanking guard: it labels any selected FrameRate, so the source projection and selection normally keep audio blank. Bella already requires blank audio Frame Rate.

MediaRate stores signed 32-bit numerator and denominator without forcing reduction. Valid means both positive. Rational equivalence is exact Int64 cross-product. Adapter keeps selected numerator/denominator as row.frameRateRatio; this is distinct from the eagerly formatted label.

Adapter converts retained ratio to double, formats three fractional digits, removes trailing zeroes and decimal point. Table and CSV reuse the stored label. Sort converts that rounded string back to double, then uses text as a tie breaker; it does not sort from frameRateRatio. It can collapse distinct fine-grained rates to one label/sort key. This is an implementation fact, not evidence the usual 23.976/25/29.97 labels are wrong.

sourceFindings.topic: FrameLayout and codec uses are separate
sourceFindings.detail: FrameLayout participates in geometry/visible-raster handling and compression naming. Current rate observation is emitted before those helpers and remains unchanged. Resolution doubles height for layout 1; that is not a rate-halving rule. Historical DNx tests include interlaced 1080i59.94 using explicit rational 30000/1001 with layout1 and half-height stored geometry.

currentMediaMuster.plainSummary: Current video projector reads own FileDescriptor.SampleRate directly and records no audio FrameRate. Current global source priority is header-first, unlike Bella agreed MDB-first policy.

Both additional 1080i50 metadata controls have FrameLayout1 and descriptor SampleRate25/1 equal to own Track.EditRate25/1. One coding label maps in current verified Compression catalogue to DV1080 50i; the other is the explicit DNxHD SQ interlaced1080 profile. These are recorded25, not50, so blindly halving because interlaced would create12.5fps.

The 13-header FrameLayout3 fractional sample is V01.E69684C0_1C5401C5406FAV.mxf with 30000/1001 in both places and DNxUncompressed coding060e2b340401010d0401020203070100. Layout alone does not imply its rational needs division by2.

These exercised descriptor/track agreements do not prove every FileDescriptor.SampleRate is universally video frames. ST377 field/coding-unit caveat remains; no sample here exercises a field-rate descriptor different from track frame clock.

proposal.status: New MXF source mapping/coverage proposed, not approved or implemented.
proposal.source: Already qualified physical video descriptor FileDescriptor.SampleRate, known complete eight-byte big-endian Rational. Preserve original signed32 numerator/denominator, both positive; source property name SampleRate, video display heading Frame Rate.
proposal.frameUnitMeaning: Use exact rate directly for supported frame-based Avid-compatible forms, including exercised interlaced controls. No universal interlace/FrameLayout halving. An unestablished field-sampled form supplies no FrameRate until a specific supported unit conversion is verified; this does not expand scope or impose a generic global conformance gate.
proposal.otherClocks: Do not substitute master/project/audio/timecode clock or infer FPS from DF mode. Own-track context can support a verified specific unit mapping where needed, not a universal alternate rate source or mandatory corroboration walk.
proposal.independence: Usable Frame Rate survives missing ContainerDuration. Preserve raw Duration unit clock unchanged if a verified variant needs a distinct frame conversion. A header rate alone does not repair MDB Duration.
proposal.sharedRepresentation: Share already-read exact descriptor fraction with Duration when units are frames; one small C++17 rate record/availability, Qt fixed-width integers and checked QtEndian reads. No permanent duplicate pair/string or new dependency solely for Frame Rate.
proposal.displayAndSort: Keep agreed late familiar labels and exact numeric sorting. Examples24/1→24,25/1→25,24000/1001→23.976,30000/1001→29.97,50/1→50,60000/1001→59.94. Uncommon label precision remains prior presentation follow-up. Never reconstruct source rate by parsing label.
proposal.audio: Visible Frame Rate stays blank, even when audio Duration has an internal display clock. AudioSamplingRate remains separate.
proposal.missingDamaged: No usable qualified supported MXF video rate means no MXF contribution; retain physical file and independent usable metadata. No invented0FPS or unrelated rate replacement.
proposal.sourcePriority: Keep usable MDB first. Only if MDB rate is unusable may a usable independently already-read own-file header contribute. Otherwise blank; no FrameRate-only media open. Overall priority/header-trigger discussion stays deferred.
proposal.retention: Release temporary bytes, ownership references and layout/coding context after extracting wanted compact facts. DF/NDF changes Duration numbering/separators, not FrameRate.
